title: Prorate accounting for hybrid prefix/KV cache hits and cross-variant batch spillover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Coalesced inference batches that contain a mix of requests with prefix cache hits, partial KV cache hits, and cache misses (including when the runtime spills requests to different model variants) are currently billed and quota-accounted in a way that overcharges or undercounts token usage for some tenants. This causes billing noise, inaccurate quota exhaustion, and throttling surprises for customers running multi-tenant or multi-model workloads.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For any coalesced batch containing N requests across M model-variants, we produce a deterministic per-request token charge calculation that sums to the total tokens processed by the runtime. 2) Partial KV/prefix cache hits result in prorated compute token charges proportional to the non-cached token delta and are clearly labeled in usage records. 3) When requests are spilled to a lower-cost variant (fallback) the metering records reflect variant-level compute and not the original requested variant. 4) Quota counters and rate-limit windows decrement in a way that customers see consistent behavior with billing CSVs and per-route dashboards. 5) New rollout passes unit/integration tests and is feature-flagged for canary.
technical_notes:
Design summary:
- At batch completion, runtime will emit two tallies: 1) raw_token_work (total decoder tokens computed across all streams) and 2) claim_shares (per-request share vector that sums to 1.0).
- For requests with prefix cache hits: mark prefix_len_cached; charge only remaining generation tokens.
- For partial KV cache hits: compute cache_hit_fraction = cached_tokens / total_requested_input_prefix; prorate input-side compute accordingly.
- For spillover to variant B from requested variant A: attribute compute tokens to variant B; create an affiliate mapping in usage records to show original request variant for customer analytics.
- Metering pipeline will create per-request usage rows using: billed_input = non_cached_input_tokens * claim_share; billed_output = output_tokens * claim_share. claim_share is normalized by per-request weight heuristic (see below).
Weight heuristic (first-pass):
- base_weight = max(1, requested_output_tokens)
- cache_penalty = 1 - cache_hit_fraction_input
- weight = base_weight * (1 + cache_penalty)
This prioritizes charging more to requests that forced actual compute.
Edge cases:
- Zero-output streams (early termination) should receive zero output charge but may still be charged for input compute if no caching.
- Strongly skewed batches (1 large request + N tiny cached requests) should never produce negative per-request charges; small cached requests will be charged the minimum unit charge and the remainder assigned to the big request.
- For multi-tenant dedicated pools, add tenant_isolation flag to enforce strict per-tenant tallies (no cross-tenant prorating).
rollout_plan: 1) Implement in metering-service feature branch with feature flag `prorate-hybrid-cache-v1`. 2) Unit tests and simulated batch generator (see qa_plan) merged. 3) Canary on low-volume region and dedicated alpha customer for 2 days. 4) Monitor discrepancies between old and new accounting metric (daily diff) and rollback if >0.5% of billed tokens deviate for more than 6 hours. 5) Gradual ramp to 100% over 48 hours with monitoring and customer comms.
qa_plan:
- Add deterministic batch simulator that can emit: purely cached batches, partially cached batches, mixed-variant spillover cases.
- Unit tests for claim_share normalization and edge case bounds.
- Integration test: end-to-end compare sum(billed_tokens) == runtime_reported_raw_token_work for 10k synthetic batches.
- Backfill script to recompute usage for 7 days of historical samples for comparison only (read-only).
